protocol.name: dashi_chrome_v1
protocol.description:
Dashi-private. Two things the standard protocols can't say.
Unified chrome (version 1): by default dashi-comp draws a title bar above every window that accepts server-side decorations. This protocol lets an app put its own content in that strip: with the "unified" style there is no title bar, the window's surface runs up to the top edge, and the compositor draws only its traffic lights (close, minimize, zoom) over the surface at the top-left.
The app moves the window itself with xdg_toplevel.move from its empty toolbar areas, and zooms it from a double click with xdg_toplevel.set_maximized / unset_maximized. A press on a traffic light goes to the compositor, never to the surface.
Glass (version 2): a surface names its panes of glass, each a rounded rectangle with a material level, and the compositor frosts what is behind them (dashi_glass_v1). The blur region of ext-background-effect-v1 says where for every compositor; these panes add what it can't: each pane's corner radius and its material. Version 3 cuts a pane to what clips it on the surface (a list scrolled past it), its shape kept. Dashi owns this file (Dashi's crates/dashi-comp/protocols/, PROTOCOL.md beside it); mirin keeps a copy.

interface.name: dashi_chrome_manager_v1

description.summary: creates window chrome controls and glass

interface.description: A global that makes a dashi_chrome_v1 for an xdg_toplevel and, from version 2, a dashi_glass_v1 for any wl_surface.

entry.name: chrome_exists
entry.summary: the toplevel already has a dashi_chrome_v1

entry.name: glass_exists
entry.summary: the surface already has a dashi_glass_v1

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the manager. Chrome objects it made stay valid.

request.name: get_chrome

description.summary: get the chrome of a toplevel

request.description: Make the chrome object of `toplevel`. A toplevel has at most one; a second request is a chrome_exists protocol error until the first is destroyed.

request.name: get_glass

description.summary: get the glass of a surface

request.description: Make the glass object of `surface`: a toplevel's, a popup's, a layer surface's or a lock surface's. A surface has at most one; a second request is a glass_exists protocol error until the first is destroyed.

interface.name: dashi_chrome_v1
interface.description:
Sets how the compositor frames one toplevel. Destroying the object puts the toplevel back to the standard style.
The style is read when the window first has a size and follows later changes, but set it before the first commit to avoid a visible shift: the compositor places the surface where the unified or standard layout puts it.

entry.name: standard
entry.summary: the compositor's title bar above the surface

entry.name: unified
entry.summary: no title bar; traffic lights over the surface

request.name: set_style
request.description: The compositor honors "unified" only for windows it would decorate itself: the toplevel has no xdg_toplevel_decoration, or its mode is server_side. An app that asked for client_side draws all of it. When the style is not honored, the controls event reports an empty rectangle.

event.name: controls

description.summary: the area of the traffic lights

event.description:
The rectangle, in surface-local logical coordinates, that the traffic lights occupy including their margins. Leave it empty (no buttons, no text) and start toolbar content past it; the compositor draws over it and takes presses in it.
Sent when the style takes effect or stops, and again when the rectangle changes (for example with the output's scale). A rectangle with zero width and height means there are no controls: the style is standard, or unified was not honored.

interface.name: dashi_glass_v1

description.summary: the panes of glass of one surface

interface.description:
A surface's panes of glass. Each pane is a rectangle in surface-local logical coordinates, its corners rounded to a radius, and a material level. The compositor draws each pane under the surface: what is behind it blurred, its colours lifted, the level's tint (raised where the words on it need it to keep their contrast), a grain, a light rim just inside its edge and a dark keel just outside. The surface paints no fill where its glass is; its translucent parts show the glass.
The panes are added back to front, in the order the surface paints them: a pane added later is drawn over one added before it (a panel on a pane that fills the surface).
The panes are double-buffered: add_pane and clear change the pending list, and wl_surface.commit applies it, in the same commit as the buffer that draws the panes' content, so glass never lags what is drawn on it. A commit with no add_pane or clear since the last one keeps the panes. After a commit the next add_pane starts a new list.
Send the same rectangles as ext_background_effect_surface_v1's blur region, for compositors without this protocol: where a surface has panes, Dashi draws its panes and does not read its blur region; a surface with a blur region and no panes is blurred there without a tint (the way other compositors do).
What a level looks like, and whether glass is frosted, shows only the wallpaper (battery saver) or is drawn solid (Reduce Transparency, a GPU that can't), is the compositor's to decide; the drawing event says whether it draws the panes at all.

entry.name: regular
entry.summary: menus, panels, banners, sheets, the launcher

entry.name: none
entry.summary: the compositor draws no glass: paint your own fill

entry.name: material
entry.summary: the compositor draws the panes: paint no fill under them

entry.name: too_many_panes
entry.summary: more than 16 panes in one commit

entry.name: invalid_pane
entry.summary: a negative size, or a radius over 512

entry.name: no_pane
entry.summary: cut_pane with no pane added since the last commit

request.name: destroy
request.description: The surface's panes go on its next commit.

request.name: add_pane

description.summary: add a pane to the pending list

request.description: A rectangle in surface-local logical coordinates, its corner radius in logical pixels (held to half its shorter side), and its level. Drawn only on the surface, its shape kept (as cut_pane). At most 16 panes a commit.

request.name: cut_pane

description.summary: show the pane added last only inside a rectangle

request.description: The pane added last shows only inside this rectangle, in surface-local logical coordinates: what clips it on the surface (a list scrolled past it). Its shape stays the whole pane's: its corners are where the pane's are, and an edge the rectangle crosses is cut straight, with neither rim nor keel there. A pane not cut shows whole. With no pane added since the last commit, a no_pane protocol error.

request.name: clear
request.description: The pending list becomes empty: the next commit removes the surface's glass.

event.name: drawing

description.summary: whether the compositor draws the panes

event.description: Sent once the object is made, and again when it changes: material when the compositor draws this surface's panes (frosted, the wallpaper only, or solid), none when it doesn't (the person turned glass off for this app, or the compositor can't). With none, paint the fill you would paint without glass.

event.name: tone
event.description: The mean colour behind the surface's first pane, blurred and lifted, before the tint, as 0xRRGGBB (sRGB): words on the glass lean toward its hue. Sent at once for a surface's new panes and to a new dashi_glass_v1 of a surface whose tone is known; then when it settles after a change, at most every 120 ms, and once a second while it keeps changing.
